title: Legendary Monster
text: “Would Keel be good, then?”
“I won’t say yes to that here. You’d probably try to arrange something in a different loop.”
Father gave some oddly noncommittal response that couldn’t exactly be called agreement.
“Let’s change the subject. But still… hmm, what would you call it. When it comes to werewolf territory, it feels like it’s in the same category as Dracula and those other Western-style monsters.”
“As I recall… vampires in this world only resemble that concept in appearance—they don’t actually have any of the classic legendary abilities, I believe.”
“Ah, I heard something about that when we visited the Siltvelt castle.”
It seemed Father had heard some talk about vampires in this world.
“Come to think of it, Wolf here is a werewolf, which means… wasn’t he supposed to be a descendant of an ancient species?”
“Wolf!”
He struck a sharp, dignified pose, showing off his werewolf form. Who was it that was fawning about in peckul form just the other day, I wonder? I daresay I’m far more charming.
“Honestly, I’m not entirely sure what makes it ‘ancient’ in practice. It doesn’t seem to be about build or anything like that.”
“Shion’s also an ancient species—or rather, a descendant of the old lizardmen—and you can tell at a glance that his build is quite different from the lizardmen of Siltvelt…”
“Indeed… I do think that myself, that I must be different from ordinary lizardmen, whenever I come to Siltvelt.”
Crocodile Guy’s beastman form was, compared to the lizardmen of Siltvelt, rather more muscular—broader, one might say. The lizardmen of Siltvelt tended to be quite slender by comparison, I say.
“Well, I suppose Shion’s a crocodile-type lizardman, while the Siltvelt lizardmen are literally lizard-type…”
“Crocodile-type… is that what you’d call it.”
“More or less, yeah. Though I also feel like there’s something dinosaur-ish about it too. I guess reptiles just tend to look similar in that regard.”
Father was smiling—whether he’d completely changed the subject on purpose or not, I couldn’t say.
“You know, I think if you put a crown and some kingly robes on Shion, with that muscular build of his, it’d actually make quite the picture. Pretty cool-looking, even.”
“What a presumptuous thing to say. Me, dressed like that?”
“Really? I think it’d suit you better than it would me…”
“No, the Shield Hero is essentially the king of Siltvelt as it stands…”
“Fair point.”
Ah, Father’s Siltvelt attire. Given his build, it does swallow him up a little, but the barbarian armor suits him well, I must say.
“My topic. It’s drifting.”
Wolf cut back in, correcting course now that the conversation had shifted to Crocodile Guy.
“Difference from ordinary species. Combat strength is different, sure, but also, the amount of power put into transforming changes the body size quite a bit.”
“Oh, right, come to think of it, Wolf, you’re pretty different now from when we first met. Even your fur color’s changed.”
“Right. And, family’s valued bloodline for generations. Looked into old records before. Traced back pretty far… but too old, so writer’s own opinions got mixed in. Hard to judge.”
“Is that so?”
“Wolf. Seems like stories of heroes from other worlds got mixed in too. Some odd things written, like how Fenrir was supposedly the progenitor.”
“Ah… well, that could happen. Wolf-types, that’s a classic pick after all.”
Father nodded, seemingly convinced by Wolf’s words. Fenrir—the famous wolf of Norse mythology. Even I know that much, I say.

“Indeed, there’s apparently talk that among demi-humans and beastmen, some can use a further skill called ‘full transformation,’ so if Wolf ever took on a complete wolf form, it’d probably look quite divine.”
“Wolf!”
Praised by Father, Wolf let out a bashful little cry.
“So, is that what you’re struggling to judge?”
“No. There’s several things, and, my lineage’s called a wolf species, but there’s also a faint story that it actually originates from youma or chimeras.”
Youma, was it? I believe I recall Ark mentioning that word before.
“Youma?”
“Yes. Same category as those creatures the heroes call vampires.”

“Ah… well, there is a story that werewolves are a kind of vampire. There’s a legend about them transforming into wolves. But Wolf, you can only transform into werewolf form, right? So maybe that doesn’t apply?”
“Old, faded book said ancient species could transform into other creatures. Hard to decipher the old text. But, probably wasted effort.”
Hmm…

“Now that I think of it, the God Slayer mentioned once that he’d come to this world quite a long time ago, back in the first world, and that an acquaintance of his had apparently settled down here. So perhaps there’s something to that, I say.”

He’d spoken of something called a Demon Beast King. Though I feel it may have had something to do with Big Sister as well. Perhaps some of Ark’s other acquaintances ended up in this world too, I daresay.
“Motoyasu-kun, you do know all sorts of things, but you always remember them at the strangest times… Can’t you recall any more detail?”
I supposed I shouldn’t tell Father too much about Ark-related matters. Similarities and such… apparently that’s a no-go, so caution was in order.
“I’m afraid I don’t know, even I,” I said.

Well, this particular matter, I couldn’t say. If Ark were here, he might tell us—though he’s the sort who’d say that even knowing wouldn’t change anything right now. He’d satisfy one’s curiosity, sure, but he’d probably add that it meant nothing, I daresay.
“Speaking of chimeras, the one that appeared during the Waves left quite an impression. Wolf doesn’t match that, though.”
“Yeah. But, there’s a lot of relatives with collars that look cool, like multiple heads.”
“That sounds more like Cerberus than a chimera, honestly.”
“In the first world, Father—driven mad by the cursed shield—modified Keel to make her like that, I say.”
“Motoyasu-kun. You’ve been on a real streak of trying to make me as uncomfortable as possible—are you aware of that?”
Father said this with great discomfort, brow furrowed.

“But that Father heard Keel’s request and granted the wish by making the modification, did he not? Furthermore, he created a new monster based on Big Sister’s hair, and transformed the village’s beloved monsters into similar forms as well, I say.”

“I keep saying this, but I really don’t think you should use me from the first world as any kind of reference… and making monsters out of Raphtalia-chan’s hair, seriously—apparently Rafumi-chan’s appearance is one result of that.”
“He was quite fond of it, I say.”
At the very least, Father had doted on the Raph-species creatures made from Big Sister’s hair.
“Setting that aside, in the mythology of my world, Cerberus and the Chimera were supposed to be siblings. Maybe those accounts got mixed together somewhere along the line?”
“Maybe so. Wolf.”
“Well, Cerberus and creatures like that do actually exist in this world. Chimeras too.”
Indeed they do. It’s a fact that if you go looking, such monsters aren’t impossible to find. After all, dragons themselves count as a kind of fantastical beast in their own right, I say.
“By that logic, does a monster called Fenrir exist too?”
Father asked everyone, wondering if anyone knew.
“Regrettably, I have never encountered one,” I said.
Having fought all manner of monsters across the world, even I had never come across a Fenrir.
“I believe it’s treated as a legendary monster that heroes speak of.”
Rabbit Guy answered. Wolf nodded in agreement.
“Doesn’t exist, huh… well, Fenrir is just a name anyway, so maybe that’s not surprising. Cerberus is also technically a name, but… it’s distinctive enough that it stands out.”
“Is Fenrir different, then? It does sound quite enormous.”

“Yeah. It’d basically be an extremely large wolf monster. In the myths, the defining trait is that it’s the wolf that killed a god, I think? If you think about it that way, if one existed, it’d have to be incredibly strong.”
“A god-slaying wolf sounds like a being that’s committed a grave sin. One could say it’s a being that kills heroes as well.”
“Ah… right, in this world, heroes are basically gods, aren’t they. Living gods, so to speak.”
Indeed, that’s the sense in which they’re worshipped, I say. Though the moment it’s inconvenient, they’re branded false heroes instead. Speaking of which, that reminded me of something.
“I’ve never encountered a Fenrir myself, but I have seen a weapon bearing the name Fenrir, I say.”
“Oh, there’s a weapon like that?”
“Indeed. Father used it, I say.”
“Eh? Me?”
Indeed. If I recalled correctly, it was the staff Father had been entrusted with when he went to face Takt in that final battle, and I’d heard that was its name.

“In the first world, when Father had the shield stolen from him by Takt, and the staff was entrusted to him as a temporary holder after it returned to the hands of Trash, who’d had a change of heart—I believe that’s when it was said to be fixed under that weapon’s name, I say.”
